raw_response:
I only have 16.1 mu, so I won't do anything fancy this year. I'll stay with cotton because that's what I know on this land, and with well water I can still manage if spring is dry. Cotton takes longer and needs more picking work, but the cash return is better for me than changing to something unfamiliar. I farm like the people around me: plant in mid to late April when the soil is warm enough, use improved seed from the local dealer, put on a base fertilizer first, then add some more when the plants start growing strongly. I cannot spend too much at once, so I will keep fertilizer at a middle level, not the heaviest rate. If the stand looks weak or yellow later, I can add a little more, but I don't want to buy too much upfront and tie up all my cash. Since I have family labor, we can handle most of the field work and picking ourselves, and only hire a little help if the picking comes all at once. With well irrigation, I plan a couple of waterings if rain is short, but I won't pump more than needed because electricity and water cost money.
